title: REFLEX: RNA Ensemble Generation via Flexibility-Calibrated Stochastic Bridge
claim: Calibrating stochastic noise per element by measured flexibility lets a generator capture diverse conformations while keeping rigid regions sharp.
layout: 3 panels: left task overview, right-top bridge, right-bottom curve; dashed dividers
description: Three-panel figure split by dashed lines. Panel a (left) shows the task. An RNA sequence box feeds an arrow labeled REFLEX. The arrow points to a 3D surface with two Gaussian peaks, one blue and one red, above a plane of scattered sample points with contours. Cartoon RNA structures in blue and red sit above the peaks to show diverse conformations. Panel b (top right) is titled SE(3) Flexibility-Calibrated Bridge. A tangled noise-prior ribbon on the left connects through a curved grid manifold to a target RNA structure on the right. The manifold carries a smooth blue path marked σ_i down and a jagged red path marked σ_i up. A B-factor colorbar runs blue to red. Panel c (bottom right) plots stochastic strength against nucleotide index. A curve dips below a dashed baseline in blue stable regions and rises above it in a red flexible region. Blue and red encode rigid versus flexible throughout.
caption: Overview of REFLEX. a: RNA ensemble generation aims to recover accurate and diverse conformational alternatives. b: Flexibility-calibrated stochastic bridge on SE(3). The structures on the right are multiple target conformations, and their averaged B-factor profile captures nucleotidewise flexibility used to calibrate the stochastic bridge. c: Nucleotide-wise stochastic strength, with nucleotides on the horizontal axis and stochasticity strength on the vertical axis; flexible positions receive stronger stochasticity than constrained positions.
abstract: RNA molecules often function through multiple experimentally observed conformational states. A central challenge is to capture ensemble diversity without sacrificing structural fidelity: samples may collapse toward averaged representative structures or drift into unsupported conformational regions. We introduce REFLEX (RNA Ensemble generation calibrated by FLEXibility), a sequence-conditioned generator for RNA backbone-frame ensembles based on a heteroscedastic stochastic bridge on SE(3). During training, experimental B-factors calibrate residue-wise bridge widths, exposing each observed conformer through local perturbation neighborhoods with residue-specific scales while keeping constrained regions sharper. A learned flexibility condition guides the bridge-field network to recover target conformer-specific frames from these calibrated noisy states. At inference, REFLEX uses only the input sequence, requiring no MSA-subsampling heuristics. On a multi-conformer RNA benchmark, REFLEX achieves the best precision-recall trade-off for ensemble coverage across evaluation thresholds, while recovery-stress ablations indicate gains in target-frame recovery under stronger perturbations.
